head: cloud/functional-harness-hash
title: test(functional): hash every module the harness imports
body:
`run.py` records `harness_sha256` so that `compare` only pairs a baseline with a candidate run from the same harness (AGENTS.md: reuse baselines only when the harness matches). The hash covered a hand-written file list. That list missed two modules the harness imports:
- `tests/functional/messages_tools.py`, imported by `openai_sdk.py` and `cache_messages_loop.py`;
- `tools/gufo/control_tokens.py`, imported by `tool_reasoning.py`.

A change to either one left the hash unchanged, so runs from different harnesses still compared as matched.

`provenance()` now hashes `harness_files()`. That is the same root list (now `HARNESS_ROOTS`) plus every local module those files import, found by walking `import`/`from` statements with `ast` and resolving them in `tests/functional/` and `tools/`. Files are hashed in sorted path order. Today this adds exactly the two files above (28 files in total). Because the hashed set changes, `harness_sha256` changes once, so existing baselines will not match runs made after this change.

`test_runner.py` gains `test_harness_hash_covers_imported_modules`.

Built in a cloud session (CPU only); Strix Halo validation pending.

> AI disclosure: I am not a software developer. Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) developed and tested this patch; this is not a claim of human developer review. Claude Code cloud session, CPU only, no GPU testing.

Test scope (Linux x86-64 cloud VM, no GPU, system Python 3):
- `python3 -m unittest test_runner.py` in `tests/functional/`: OK. The new test errors on unpatched main (`harness_files` is missing).
- `cmake --preset cpu-test && cmake --build --preset pr --parallel 4`: 54/54 hosted tests passed, including `functional_runner_test`.
- `tools/ci/check-pr-title.py`: PASS. No live functional suite ran; none is needed to exercise the hash.
